name: My Tho food guide
summary: Mỹ Tho eats hủ tiếu at breakfast, lunch, and supper, dry or with broth, from strands of local Gò Cát rice. Cross to Thới Sơn for fried elephant-ear fish and straw-fired snakehead in the orchards, then finish at the night court on the pier with chè and shellfish.
body: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is the town’s bowl: rice strands that smell of rice and stay soft, topped with minced pork and crackling, and seasoned at the table with soy, lime, sugar, and chili or satay. The provincial and national tourism sites date its fame to the early 1960s, Vietnam Tourism’s noodle-village article goes back to Hoa cooks at the end of the 19th century, and the city portal claims a hundred years. The national site eats it without lettuce, vinegar, or herbs, while the village article adds fresh greens to the soup bowl. The same village names hủ tiếu sa tế and hủ tiếu xương beside the dry and soup bowls.

On cù lao Thới Sơn, about 6 km across the river, the orchard table brings fried elephant-ear fish, grilled shrimp, linh-fish mắm hotpot with điên điển flowers, straw-fired snakehead, mussel bánh xèo, and green-skin pomelo salad. Ginger honey tea, handmade coconut candy, and fruit off the trees come with the music. The Tiền Giang provincial portal and Mia, 25 Sep 2023, cook the snakehead two different ways, and both are below.

Back on the mainland, the Mỹ Phong noodle village makes bánh tét, bánh ít, bánh hỏi, and bánh tầm beside its hủ tiếu. The night court inside the tourist-boat pier on đường 30 Tháng 4 serves chè, sinh tố, sâm bổ lượng, nghêu, and sò: 18:30–02:00 in a 5 Jan 2019 provincial article, or from 18:00 and busiest 19:00–22:00 on Viet Fun Travel. Mắm tôm chà, mắm còng, and bánh giá belong to Gò Công, Tân Phú Đông, and Chợ Giồng, so eat them there.
specialtiesLead: Start with a bowl of hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho, then take the boat to the Thới Sơn orchard table. The Mỹ Phong cakes, the pier-court sweets and shellfish, and the plates from Gò Công follow.

sections.heading: The Thới Sơn table
paragraphs: Take the boat to cù lao Thới Sơn, about 6 km from town, and eat at the orchard stop around midday. The fish, the hotpot, and the salads come to the same table as the fruit, the tea, and the music.

spots.name: Ca tai tuong chien xu
spots.note: A whole elephant-ear fish soaked in salt water, then fried golden in plenty of oil. Roll it with herbs, rice paper, and bún, and dip it in mắm nêm or nước mắm me.

spots.name: Tom nuong moi
spots.note: Grilled shrimp, served beside the fried elephant-ear fish.

spots.name: Lau mam ca linh
spots.nameVi: Lẩu mắm cá linh bông điên điển
spots.note: A shared hotpot of mắm with linh fish and điên điển flowers.

spots.name: Ca loc nuong trui
spots.note: Field snakehead cooked under burning straw, about 5 minutes on the provincial portal, or uncleaned and fired until it smells done in Mia’s account. Peel off the charred skin and roll the meat with rice paper, bún, herbs, unripe banana, and cucumber.

spots.name: Canh chua ca loc
spots.note: A sour-sweet snakehead soup with fish sauce and sliced chili, common across the South and eaten with white rice.

spots.name: Banh xeo nhan hen
spots.note: A bánh xèo pancake filled with hến mussels.

spots.name: Goi buoi da xanh
spots.note: A salad of green-skin pomelo, served with the fish and the hotpot.

spots.name: Xoi chien phong
spots.note: Sticky rice pounded with garlic and turned in boiling oil until it puffs into a taut ball. It usually comes with roast chicken or gà xối mỡ.

spots.name: Thoi Son orchard fruit
spots.note: Longan, rambutan, xoài cát Hòa Lộc, and mận An Phước. Pick and eat in the orchard, or buy some to take.

spots.name: Tra mat ong gung
spots.note: Ginger tea sweetened with the islet’s OCOP honey, poured in the orchard while the musicians play. A Zing account says the hives on Lân and Phụng feed on longan blossom.

spots.name: Keo dua
spots.note: Handmade coconut candy, sold with the honey as one of the islet’s OCOP products. Cồn Phụng, across the river in Ben Tre, makes it too.

sections.heading: Mỹ Phong village cakes
paragraphs: The Mỹ Phong craft village is where the hủ tiếu strands are made, and it turns out these cakes and bowls beside the noodle. The Hội Gia noodle yards open 07:00–18:00.

spots.name: Banh tet
spots.address: Ấp Hội Gia, phường Mỹ Phong
spots.note: One of the cakes the noodle village makes beside its hủ tiếu.

spots.name: Banh it
spots.address: Ấp Hội Gia, phường Mỹ Phong
spots.note: One of the small cakes the village makes beside bánh tét.

spots.name: Banh hoi
spots.address: Ấp Hội Gia, phường Mỹ Phong
spots.note: Mỹ Phong’s own bánh hỏi, distinct from the Phong Điền kind.

spots.name: Banh tam
spots.address: Ấp Hội Gia, phường Mỹ Phong
spots.note: One of the rice products the village makes beside its hủ tiếu.

spots.name: Hu tieu sa te
spots.note: The satay version of the town’s rice-noodle bowl, eaten beside the soup and dry bowls.

spots.name: Hu tieu xuong
spots.note: The bone bowl of Mỹ Tho hủ tiếu, eaten beside the satay and dry versions.

sections.heading: Pier-court orders
paragraphs: The night court inside the tourist-boat pier also serves hủ tiếu, bún, phở, cháo, bánh cuốn, and dried seafood. These are the light orders and the shellfish it is known for: 18:30–02:00 in a 5 Jan 2019 provincial article, or from 18:00 and busiest 19:00–22:00 on Viet Fun Travel.

spots.name: Sam bo luong
spots.note: One of the light orders, served beside chè and sinh tố.

spots.name: Che
spots.note: A light sweet order for after the riverside walk.

spots.name: Sinh to
spots.note: A smoothie, one of the light orders beside chè and sâm bổ lượng.

spots.name: Ngheu
spots.note: Clams, one of the shellfish the court is known for. Order a plate to share.

spots.name: So
spots.note: Sò shellfish, served beside the nghêu and the dried seafood.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These three belong to other towns of the old Tiền Giang province, so plan to eat them there. Mắm tôm chà is Gò Công, mắm còng is Tân Phú Đông or cù lao Tân Thới, and bánh giá is Chợ Giồng in Gò Công Tây.

spots.name: Mam tom cha
spots.note: Pounded shrimp paste eaten with bún, boiled pork, unripe banana, sour starfruit, cucumber, and herbs. Thanh Niên, 27 Aug 2014, says the dip should balance sour, sweet, hot, and salty.

spots.name: Mam cong
spots.address: Tân Phú Đông, or cù lao Tân Thới
spots.note: A crab paste, best when made from peeled crab. The provincial portal places it at Tân Phú Đông in its food index and at cù lao Tân Thới in its 25 Dec 2018 introduction.

spots.name: Banh gia Cho Giong
spots.note: A fried cake of rice and bean batter with bean sprouts, pork, shrimp, and peanuts. The provincial portal uses mung bean, while Tuổi Trẻ uses three parts rice to one part soy.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The pier court is the place to eat after dark. Hội Gia is where you watch the noodle sheets made, and Chợ Mỹ Tho is a short ride inland from đường 30 Tháng 4.

spots.name: Pier food court
spots.nameVi: Khu ẩm thực đêm Mỹ Tho
spots.address: Đường 30 Tháng 4, inside the tourist-boat pier
spots.note: A 3,000 m² night court beside the Tiền, open 18:30–02:00 in a 5 Jan 2019 provincial article. Viet Fun Travel lists a night market at số 8 đường 30/4 from 18:00, busiest 19:00–22:00.

spots.name: Hoi Gia noodle yards
spots.address: Ấp Hội Gia, phường Mỹ Phong
spots.note: Watch the rice sheets rolled, dried, and cut, free, 07:00–18:00, for about 120 minutes. Eat the bowl in town afterward.

spots.name: My Tho market
spots.note: The town market, about 10 minutes by vehicle from đường 30 Tháng 4.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Start the day with hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho, which the old phường 9 ward office calls a breakfast, lunch, and supper bowl. Order it dry, or with the broth poured over.

seoTitle: My Tho food — hu tieu and the Thoi Son table
seoDescription: Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho dry or with broth, fried elephant-ear fish and straw-fired snakehead on Thới Sơn, Mỹ Phong cakes, and chè and shellfish at the pier court.
